Bird Flu strikes an already struggling poultry industry

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Poultry Farms look like toxic waste sites, farm workers have hazmat suits and have to go through several de-contamination chambers entering and leaving the poultry farms. Vehicles are sprayed and they have become no go zones. Bird flu strain H5N8 has struck and its the most deadly bird flu virus to hit SA so far rapidly spreading across the country. Currently there is no vaccine in the country and no insurance or compensation for farmers. 1 Million birds have been culled by the end of August and the figure is rising. Its hit 35 farms across the country 15 of which are commercial farms. Entire flocks are dying over night and although people cannot get sick from the virus, workers are loosing their jobs.

Summary:
10 days ago Duck farmer Leon Groeneveld had a thriving Duck business. He had just received a huge order from the Seychelles and Pick and Pay had agreed to supply whole frozen ducks in it's stores. After 8 years of working very hard to expand his duck business things were looking good. Then overnight 11000 of his ducks dropped dead. Bird Flu had struck. Then on his parent breeding stock farm 5 kms away the ducks stopped laying eggs- from 1200 eggs a day to 234. They too had the flu. Yesterday he slaughtered 35 000 of his ducks, most perfectly healthy but his farm is under quarantine and there is nothing he can do with them. The parent breeding stock also had to be culled and for the next for 45 days his farm is a no go area as is every farm within a 5 km radius in the hopes it will control the virus from spreading. But its wild birds that are the biggest danger and you can't stop them and so we have seen the disease move from Zimbabwe through Limpopo right down to the Western Cape. “It’s like being hit by a train”



Further information:
Bird flu or Avian flu is like human flu and occurs every winter. However this year’s strain H5N8 is extremely vicious and it’s hitting the large as well as the small producers. Bird flu is carried by wild birds that migrate from the north carrying the disease and this last winter there was a lot of bird flu in Europe.
Currently in South Africa there is no vaccination for this virus and like all viruses they mutate each year so even if we did vaccinate it won’t protect us next year. It also has trade implications and is only effective on longer living birds like egg production and parent breeding stock.
Currently they want to import fertilised eggs but that carries disease risks and we are not geared up to do this. Production cycles are planned two years in advance and with parent stock wiped out it has massive knock on implications. Its also vital that they maintain their place in the market because they are already under pressure of cheap imports and “Dumping” For example imported Duck cost R27 kilogram but it cost R45 to produce locally.
There is also no insurance against bird flu so when your entire stock gets wiped out there is nothing you can do- the farm is under quarantine for 3 months and has to be declared virus free before any production can happen. The only way to protect your birds is through strict bio control measures and air condition sheds. Even workers that change boots, shower and change clothing when walking from shower to shed can step on wild bird dropping an carry the disease into the sheds. Wild birds can contaminate water sources and so water supply has to be chlorinated but even that is not fool proof.
Even the big producers with stringent bio controls have been hit. Astal foods parent stock was hit in June and the entire flock culled costing Astal 50 million rand so far. This all comes on the back of 5 very tough years in the poultry industry with the price of maize increasing because of the drought, cheap imports being ”dumped” a weakening rand and now Bird Flu wiping out entire flocks.
The larger producers can rotate their workers but the smaller producers can’t, Leon Groenveld has to retrench 96 highly skilled workers and is hoping somehow when he is on his feet again he can reemploy them and they will still be available.
Poultry farming is promoted by DAFF as a poverty relief mechanism but it’s the smaller farmers that are the hardest hit and ironically Free range birds and birds that have fresh air circulating through their enclosures are the most at risk.
Its a notifiable disease and all infected birds have to be destroyed and the burden of disposal is placed on the farmers with no assistance from the State. The State Veterinary services which are already stretched to the limit are trying to educate poultry farmers and co-ordinate a response to the outbreak and increase farmers bio control but with 100 of 1000's of backyard chicken owners its a loosing battle.
The Western cape is the latest to be hit. We will speak to State Vets, affected farms as well as free range farmers and egg producers who have not been effected about what they are doing to protect their flocks and the increasing cost of such measures

Press Release:


Bird Flu Strikes Again
Poultry Farms look like toxic waste sites; workers wear safety gear and have to go through several
decontamination chambers before entering and leaving the farms. Bird flu strain H5N8 has struck and it’s
the most deadly bird flu virus to hit the commercial poultry industry. For smaller players like duck farmer
Leon Groeneveld, this outbreak has been crippling. Carte Blanche asks: what does the future hold for the
already embattled poultry industry?

Script:


Script: South Africans eat 37 kilo’s of chicken per person per year; it’s the most affordable and popular protein, so when a flu epidemic hits the poultry industry it affects us all
Link “Almost every year there are outbreaks of Avian flu but this strain is extremely aggressive and more than a million birds have had to be culled already
Script: It’ struck both large and small producers across the country, the worst outbreak is in the Western Cape first striking 46 Ostrich farms and then onto the densely populated poultry areas. Duck farmer Leon Groeneveld lost his entire flock of 35 000 ducks
Leon Groeneveld 01 34 56 00 I have invested all my assets I had into the duck farm and I am walking out here with basically nothing I will have to see how I can settle all our debts
Script: Leon was an Insurance broker before he bought The Duck farm 8 years ago. Things were looking up- they had a contract in the Seychelles and a large local retailer was about to supply whole ducks in their stores
Leon Groeneveld 01 27 10 08. We have got two farms the one is where we grow the ducks those were culled first then we tested our breeders and they were also H5 positive So basically there is no provision of eggs to produce ducks so everything is gone.
Script: This virus doesn’t infect people but we can carry it on our shoes if we have stepped in infected faeces
Link: “We can’t go onto the Duck farm it’s been put under quarantine for the next few months and this has happened to nearly 40 farms across the country in fact it’s almost impossible to go onto any poultry farm because of the extremely strict controls against infection
Link “It is the first time that commercial poultry farms have been hit by highly pathogenic avian flu and it has the potential to have a devastating effect on the industry
Script: CEO of the South African Poultry Association and qualified vet Dr Charlotte Nkuna explained why this is such a concern
Charlotte “Highly pathogenic means that particular strain that would kill a lot of chickens in a very short space of time
Derek “So it’s a more aggressive strain
Charlotte “this is the first deadly strain of bird flu that we have had in chickens we have had in ostriches and for all those outbreaks they never really jumped onto chickens it was a matter of time for many years because other countries have had it over and over
Script: Astral foods is the largest chicken producer in the country and has extremely high bio security. Two of their breeder farms were struck- they’re the parents that generate the eggs to produce the chicken that land on our plates. Gary Arnold says they were doing all they could
Gary “there is controlled people movement there is controlled movement of equipment and vehicles onto site people have to shower in and out of those facilities
Script: This strain of bird flu H5N8 originated in Asia. Migrating birds have carried the virus across the globe. They’ve infected local wild bird populations which don’t have immunity to the virus and in turn they have infected poultry, ostriches and even pigs
Gary “From Oct of 2016 to end of May June of this year Europe confirmed over 2700 confirmed cases of infection both of wild birds and in domestic poultry across 27 countries
Script: To date it’s cost Astral 50 million rand and close to half a million birds.
Gary “removing those birds from the farm there is long replacement cycle repopulating that farm and we expect it will take us at least 18 months to re stock both of those farms
Script: Leon is still adding up the costs - it will take 10 months before he can hope to see the first duckling. He has no means of supporting his staff of 96
Derek “It must have been difficult telling your staff you couldn’t employ them
Leon Groeneveld “my staff work with me they don’t work for me I can’t do anything without them they are my biggest asset. That day was the worst day for me, it felt like I was in a dream world and I was going to wake up any minute
Script: Julia Andrews worked in the hatchery for the last 13 years
“For me it was a big shock because now we sit without work we are a family many of us don’t have an income this was our last income
Script: The worst part for everyone was culling 35 000 of their own birds, both the sick and healthy
Julia “we had to kill all the ducks, throw away the eggs the eggs that were in the incubators we put on high and burnt and died so that we could get rid of everything. It’s a heart breaking story.
Script: There is a 3 km quarantine radius around infected farms
Gary 04 27 38 12 if you are a neighbour to an infected farm and you are very close to that farm it could impact you. Between the houses on the farm that we have had the confirmed cases we firmly believe it became airborne…. it did spread amongst the houses no matter what measures we tried to take
Script: The cost of culling the birds and disposing of them by composting them on the farm is borne by the farmer. All that the Department of Agriculture does is to check that the temperature of the compost rises to 50 degrees for 3 consecutive days, killing the virus
Leon: Just the breeder ducks the value was 1.6 million. There is no compensation there is no insurance that pays
Derek’ Is there any finalization on the issue of compensation from the Department
Charlotte “this is not something they would normally put in their budget so they would then have to put in a proposal or an application in to Treasury so it’s quite a lengthy process
Script: There almost 200 000 backyard chickens in the Western Cape alone and without compensation farmers have no incentive to inform the state and could possibly dispose of infected hens despite the heavy penalties this carries.
Gary “if producers are assured of some form of compensation perhaps they will react quicker if they suspect that their birds are infected without compensation they may adopt the wait and see approach.
Script: Dr Aileen Pyper the Western Cape Provincial State Vet for the Boland region is extremely concerned and is trying to inform all bird owners about the risks
Aileen “we are appealing to all bird owners to increase their bio security measures… you want restrict contact with wild birds you want people to observe good hygienic practices you want to limit movement of people animals and vehicles onto your property 02 50 02 04 but we definitely don’t want the message to be that people should start shooting wild birds because…….if you shoot wild birds you create a vacuum in that area and other wild birds start to move in
Script: Birds kept in aviaries, homing pigeons and free range farms are all at risk of contact with wild birds. Even the Vergnoegd wine farm which uses runner ducks to organically control snails in the vineyards is worried
Link “at this time of day the ducks would normally be chilling on the dam but with the avian flu epidemic Peter can’t take the risk of them interacting with the wild birds
Script: Peter Stuart Managing Director says they are extremely concerned to protect their flock of 1200 ducks and the poultry industry around them
Peter “we are in this extremely sensitive period we are keeping them more into the yard they are not allowed to go into the vineyards they are very restricted from away from wild birds as possible in the sort of distressing phase we probably will have to resort to keeping them indoors with nets over them and then as and when this epidemic blows over we will be able to put them back into the vineyards again
Script: But to keep the ducks and the visitors happy they still get to do their parade twice a day keeping up their training of walking in line and delighting the spectators. With summer around the corner the high temperatures will kill off the virus, but currently things are not looking good.
Gary “it is a very serious risk it’s a highly contagious disease and it poses a severe risk to the local poultry industry, food security is paramount in SA and any further impacts in the poultry industry itself will lead to short supply of product.

Even the Vergnoegd wine farm which uses runner ducks to organically control snails in the vineyards is worried Link “at this time of day the ducks would normally be chilling on the dam but with the avian flu epidemic Peter can’t take the risk of them interacting with the wild birds Script: Peter Stuart Managing Director says they are extremely concerned to protect their flock of 1200 ducks and the poultry industry around them Peter “we are in this extremely sensitive period we are keeping them more into the yard they are not allowed to go into the vineyards they are very restricted from away from wild birds as possible in the sort of distressing phase we probably will have to resort to keeping them indoors with nets over them and then as and when this epidemic blows over we will be able to put them back into the vineyards again Script: But to keep the ducks and the visitors happy they still get to do their parade twice a day keeping up their training of walking in line and delighting the spectators. With summer around the corner the high temperatures will kill off the virus, but currently things are not looking good. Gary “it is a very serious risk it’s a highly contagious disease and it poses a severe risk to the local poultry industry, food security is paramount in SA and any further impacts in the poultry industry itself will lead to short supply of product. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Poultry Farms look like toxic waste sites, farm workers have hazmat suits and have to go through several de-contamination chambers entering and leaving the poultry farms. Vehicles are sprayed and they have become no go zones. Bird flu strain H5N8 has struck and its the most deadly bird flu virus to hit SA so far rapidly spreading across the country. Currently there is no vaccine in the country and no insurance or compensation for farmers. 1 Million birds have been culled by the end of August and the figure is rising. Its hit 35 farms across the country 15 of which are commercial farms. Entire flocks are dying over night and although people cannot get sick from the virus, workers are loosing their jobs.
metadata.Summary: 10 days ago Duck farmer Leon Groeneveld had a thriving Duck business. He had just received a huge order from the Seychelles and Pick and Pay had agreed to supply whole frozen ducks in it's stores. After 8 years of working very hard to expand his duck business things were looking good. Then overnight 11000 of his ducks dropped dead. Bird Flu had struck. Then on his parent breeding stock farm 5 kms away the ducks stopped laying eggs- from 1200 eggs a day to 234. They too had the flu. Yesterday he slaughtered 35 000 of his ducks, most perfectly healthy but his farm is under quarantine and there is nothing he can do with them. The parent breeding stock also had to be culled and for the next for 45 days his farm is a no go area as is every farm within a 5 km radius in the hopes it will control the virus from spreading. But its wild birds that are the biggest danger and you can't stop them and so we have seen the disease move from Zimbabwe through Limpopo right down to the Western Cape. “It’s like being hit by a train”
metadata.Further information: Bird flu or Avian flu is like human flu and occurs every winter. However this year’s strain H5N8 is extremely vicious and it’s hitting the large as well as the small producers. Bird flu is carried by wild birds that migrate from the north carrying the disease and this last winter there was a lot of bird flu in Europe. Currently in South Africa there is no vaccination for this virus and like all viruses they mutate each year so even if we did vaccinate it won’t protect us next year. It also has trade implications and is only effective on longer living birds like egg production and parent breeding stock. Currently they want to import fertilised eggs but that carries disease risks and we are not geared up to do this. Production cycles are planned two years in advance and with parent stock wiped out it has massive knock on implications. Its also vital that they maintain their place in the market because they are already under pressure of cheap imports and “Dumping” For example imported Duck cost R27 kilogram but it cost R45 to produce locally. There is also no insurance against bird flu so when your entire stock gets wiped out there is nothing you can do- the farm is under quarantine for 3 months and has to be declared virus free before any production can happen. The only way to protect your birds is through strict bio control measures and air condition sheds. Even workers that change boots, shower and change clothing when walking from shower to shed can step on wild bird dropping an carry the disease into the sheds. Wild birds can contaminate water sources and so water supply has to be chlorinated but even that is not fool proof. Even the big producers with stringent bio controls have been hit. Astal foods parent stock was hit in June and the entire flock culled costing Astal 50 million rand so far. This all comes on the back of 5 very tough years in the poultry industry with the price of maize increasing because of the drought, cheap imports being ”dumped” a weakening rand and now Bird Flu wiping out entire flocks. The larger producers can rotate their workers but the smaller producers can’t, Leon Groenveld has to retrench 96 highly skilled workers and is hoping somehow when he is on his feet again he can reemploy them and they will still be available. Poultry farming is promoted by DAFF as a poverty relief mechanism but it’s the smaller farmers that are the hardest hit and ironically Free range birds and birds that have fresh air circulating through their enclosures are the most at risk. Its a notifiable disease and all infected birds have to be destroyed and the burden of disposal is placed on the farmers with no assistance from the State. The State Veterinary services which are already stretched to the limit are trying to educate poultry farmers and co-ordinate a response to the outbreak and increase farmers bio control but with 100 of 1000's of backyard chicken owners its a loosing battle. The Western cape is the latest to be hit. We will speak to State Vets, affected farms as well as free range farmers and egg producers who have not been effected about what they are doing to protect their flocks and the increasing cost of such measures
